first_impression.reaction: Googled 'same sex marriage greece' half expecting a rainbow-washed sales page. First word is 'Yes', then a date it's been in force, then 'check the steps with the municipality... and with the Australian Embassy in Athens' before booking a venue. That's a straight answer and a limit in the first two paragraphs. I jumped to the FAQ, then the documents and recognition sections. Law number, the exact Civil Code wording, links to the gazette text, DFAT, Smartraveller and the AG's department. It even repeats Smartraveller's warning about homophobic attacks, which a pure marketing page would bury. My main gap: the only worked example is Rhodes, and the two islands people actually ask about get 'check with the municipality'.

journey.quote: Before you book a venue, check the steps with the municipality where you will marry and with the Australian Embassy in Athens.
journey.reaction: Telling me to check with government before I pay anyone. That's not an upsell. Good start.

journey.quote: When the legal route is clear, [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=same-sex-marriage-greece&utm_content=primary) and plan the celebration around it.
journey.reaction: Booking link before the article has proved anything. It's conditional and soft, so minor, but evidence first, then the ask.

journey.section: Is same-sex marriage legal in Greece?
journey.quote: Article 1350 now reads: "Marriage is contracted between two persons of different or the same sex. Marriage requires the agreement of the intending spouses."
journey.reaction: The actual statutory wording, the law number and a link to the text. That's the kind of thing I can check myself, and it holds up as a source.

journey.quote: It states no residency or nationality condition of its own, and neither the law nor the Ministry of Interior circular sets out how a foreign national's freedom to marry is assessed.
journey.reaction: Admits the law doesn't answer my question rather than pretending it does. Honest about the gap.

journey.section: Civil ceremony at the town hall
journey.quote: Hold the next working day free, and keep your departure flights well clear of it.
journey.reaction: Concrete, practical, and it follows from the Rhodes sign-the-next-day rule. Goes in the spreadsheet.

journey.quote: Other islands may ask for more, or for less.
journey.reaction: Fair caveat, but it means the only checklist on the page is for Rhodes. If I'm marrying on Santorini I still don't know what to file.

journey.quote: DFAT can also issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so ask first whether yours must come from Athens and whether it needs an apostille.
journey.reaction: That's the catch I'd have found the hard way. Flagged before I wasted a trip to DFAT.

journey.section: Will your Greek marriage be recognised in Australia?
journey.quote: Your Greek marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but may not work as proof of a change of name, so check that with your state or territory registry of births, deaths and marriages.
journey.reaction: A limitation stated plainly, with who to ask. No pretending it's all sorted.

journey.section: What the law covers, and what it does not
journey.quote: Couples declare their future children's surname before the wedding, to a notary or to the officiant, who must ask for it.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that and wouldn't have thought to look. Useful.

journey.section: Is Greece LGBT friendly for a destination wedding?
journey.quote: Racially motivated and homophobic attacks have occurred.
journey.reaction: A company selling Greek weddings quoting the government warning straight. That's the single line that makes me believe the rest.

journey.quote: Confirm the civil ceremony steps and settings with the island's municipality before you hold a date.
journey.reaction: So for the island most people actually want, there's nothing specific. Honest, but thin compared with the Rhodes detail.

journey.quote: A venue that welcomes same-sex weddings will say so without hesitation.
journey.reaction: Says who? It's a fair rule of thumb but it's stated like a fact.

journey.quote: Have you hosted same-sex weddings before, and will you put that in writing?
journey.reaction: The right question, in writing. The whole list is stuff I'd actually send.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments around your civil ceremony, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins;
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing' is the right signal. Still doesn't say whether venues pay them a cut, but that's a call question.

journey.section: Legal ceremony, symbolic celebration or both
journey.quote: Whichever you choose, remember the rule on recognition.
journey.reaction: Three options laid out with the trade-off tied back to the law. Clear enough to decide on.

journey.section: Plan your Greece wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it, from the island and the venue to your guests' rooms and the long dinner after, is ours to plan.
journey.reaction: Brochure voice creeping in at the end. Harmless, I skip it.

unanswered_questions: What do Santorini and Mykonos municipalities actually ask for, and where will their registrars officiate? The only worked example is Rhodes.
End to end, how far ahead do we need to start the paperwork, given the CNI is valid for six months and the embassy needs appointments?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real same-sex wedding in Greece you've planned that I can look at, with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: When the legal route is clear, [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=same-sex-marriage-greece&utm_content=primary) and plan the celebration around it.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA before any evidence. It's conditional so it's minor, but I want proof before the ask.

turn_offs_found.quote: A venue that welcomes same-sex weddings will say so without hesitation.
turn_offs_found.why: An assertion with nothing behind it, sitting in a page that otherwise sources everything. It reads as opinion dressed as fact.

turn_offs_found.quote: Some couples keep the civil ceremony small, with the two witnesses and close family, and hold the larger celebration that evening or the next day.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Some couples' is a generalisation with no source. Probably true, but it's the kind of line I discount.

turn_offs_found.quote: Everything around it, from the island and the venue to your guests' rooms and the long dinner after, is ours to plan.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sales copy instead of facts. The tone I skip.

would_share_with: My partner, the documents list and the 'What Australians arrange' section
Our guests, the Smartraveller safety paragraph with the itinerary

cta_reaction.why: The page earned it: real law, real sources, the homophobic-attack warning left in, and 'fee agreed in writing'. I'd still want to know whether venues pay them before handing over details, and I'd want island-specific paperwork for Santorini or Mykonos, but I'd take a call.

top_3_changes: Give Santorini and Mykonos the same treatment as Rhodes, or say plainly that their municipalities don't publish a list. 'Confirm the civil ceremony steps and settings with the island's municipality before you hold a date.' leaves the most-searched islands with nothing concrete.
Add a rough end-to-end lead time for the paperwork (CNI, translation, apostille, embassy appointment), sourced or framed as a checklist, so I can plan backwards from a date.

Soften or attribute unsupported generalisations: 'A venue that welcomes same-sex weddings will say so without hesitation.' and 'Some couples keep the civil ceremony small'. Optionally move the primary CTA below the legal section so evidence comes before the ask.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for catches, flagged unsupported claims
No invented brand facts; commission and real-budget questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
No prices and no named venues not penalised; deferred business details and transfers not must-fix; no sourcing requests beyond the page's own wording

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold any Santorini or Mykonos municipal requirements? If not, should the page say they are not published?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'same sex marriage greece' while comparing three planners and is planning a same-sex wedding with his partner, so relevance is 4.
No prices and no named venues are deliberate and not penalised.
Municipal descriptions of ceremony locations (e.g. Lindos) are attributed to the municipality, not counted as brand claims.
